In [[applied mathematics]], a '''doubly linked face list''' ('''DLFL''') is an efficient [[data structure]] for storing [[Topological manifold|2-manifold]] mesh data.  The structure stores [[linked list]]s for a 3D mesh's faces, edges, vertices, and corners. The structure guarantees the preservation of the [[manifold]] property.<ref>{{citation
 | last = Chen | first = Jianer
 | doi = 10.1016/S0304-3975(96)00273-3
 | issue = 2
 | journal = [[Theoretical Computer Science (journal)|Theoretical Computer Science]]
 | mr = 1465274
 | pages = 247–266
 | title = Algorithmic graph embeddings
 | volume = 181
 | year = 1997| doi-access = free
 }}.</ref><ref>{{citation
 | last1 = dos Santos | first1 = Thiago R.
 | last2 = Meinzer | first2 = Hans-Peter
 | last3 = Maier-Hein | first3 = Lena
 | doi = 10.1142/S0218195911003767
 | issue = 4
 | journal = International Journal of Computational Geometry & Applications
 | mr = 2826033
 | pages = 467–494
 | title = Extending the doubly linked face list for the representation of 2-pseudomanifolds and 2-manifolds with boundaries
 | volume = 21
 | year = 2011}}.</ref>
